question_type: Absolute difference of two within-year Pearson correlations (Treasury vs New Aa corporate monthly long-term yields) for 1979 and 1984, 4 dp

opus_divergence.what_opus_did: Mapped all three definitions of the Treasury column: the pre-1983 composite, the 1983-86 20-yr constant maturity series, and the 30-yr series used from Sept 1986 and restated back to 1977. Opus chose the latest printing, the 30-yr series (1986_09 to 1991_03), because the Bulletin calls the switch a 'revision'. It cited the question's example value, which appears only in 1988+ tables, as weak support. It computed the 20-yr alternative and noted that it changes the 4-dp answer.
opus_divergence.what_right_glm_did: The prompt arm took 1984 from the March 1985 issue (20-yr series) and 1979 from the March 1980 issue (old composite series), and never looked past the 1985_06 issue. At 4 dp its result coincides with the 20-yr and mixed-vintage alternatives that Opus listed and rejected.
opus_divergence.evidence: Opus: worklog.md:45-50 (30-yr vintage); worklog.md:52-64 (candidate table and vintage choice); solution.json decisions[0]; review.md section 3 (residual risk: 20-yr vintage). GLM prompt digest: [9]-[13], [16], [17]. The full text of [13] in events.jsonl says 'Could use that single vintage' and later 'These match 1985_03 panel 3', although only the corporate column matched.

reviewer_flag: Verdict confirmed. The reviewer flagged the superseded 20-yr vintage as the only residual risk, and noted that the section heading 'Average Yields of Long-Term Bonds' covers issues from both vintages.
right_by_principled_choice_or_luck: Luck. The prompt arm built a mixed-vintage pair (old-composite 1979 Treasury values with 20-yr 1984 Treasury values) after wrongly asserting at [13] that the 1979 values in 1980_03 and 1985_03 match; only the corporate column matched. Its own adapter text says to grep the row forward and use the latest vintage until a family has been checked (AGENTS.md:1674-1676). It did not do that. Had it done so, it would have reached the 30-yr series, as Opus and cards did. Both its mixed pair and a consistent 20-yr pair round to the same 4-dp value.
wrong_glm_arms_same_as_opus: cards: yes. It grepped forward to the last AY-1 printing that carries both years (1987_12, 30-yr series) and submitted the same result as Opus ([25]-[44]). none: no. It used the 1985_03 table but assigned the year panels wrongly from the shifted year-label row: at [13] it took the 1973 block as 1979 and the 1982 block as 1984, ending >25pct off.
lesson_for_harness: The 'latest revision' default is wrong when a later printing changes the definition of the series (20-yr constant maturity to 30-yr), even though the Bulletin calls the change a revision. For at least 1984, the key used the pre-switch 20-yr printing, most plausibly the first issue containing both requested years in one table (March 1985). Candidate rule: when a column header or footnote definition changes between printings, prefer the printing whose definition was current when the requested periods were first fully published (or the earliest single table covering all of them). Treat definition changes differently from numeric revisions. Weak textual clues, such as the example value in the question, should not override this rule.
notes: The corporate series is identical in every vintage; only the Treasury column changes definition. The 4-dp answer is very sensitive to that change, because both correlations are near 0.99 and differ only in the third decimal. Together with ordinal 4 (key = latest printing) and ordinal 36 (key = first printing, disputed), this shows that no single recency rule reproduces the keys. A harness should surface the vintage fork explicitly and choose by whether the series definition fits the requested period, not by recency alone. The prompt arm used only 10 requests here, and its correctness is not evidence that its procedure works.
